I hate to get gloom and doom about single payer because the concept is solid-- the problem is that we keep approaching it the wrong way. You can't have for-profit hospitals and for-profit insurance snatching as big a margin as they can every step of the way alongside state-sponsored health care. It's been nothing but a disaster for Obamacare, and it will be nothing but a disaster if not implemented differently by Sander's plan.

In countries where single payer works, the government plan sets the rules and MUST negotiate for the best deal it can for all of the people covered-- and because the hospital has no choice but to cave to their demands or lose all of its business, they have to bow to the pressure. The greater the portion of people covered under their plan, the greater collective bargaining power the government holds to bring down prices, the less money they need for taxes to run the program.
